evidence: Receiving DO2 at 48.0h: 11.51 mg/L; 48.2h: 5.31 mg/L; 52.0h: 4.35 mg/L (simulated online sensor)
Source batches 1-3 DO2 at ~48-52h remain 10.5-11.3 mg/L (e.g., source-1 52.0h: 10.88 mg/L)
Receiving P assay 48.0h: 2.609 g/L, on trajectory vs source batches 2.98-3.06 g/L
Minimum DO constraint 2.0 mg/L; current DO2 4.35 mg/L and trending downward
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11.5 to ~4.4-5.3 mg/L between 48.0 and 52.0 h, far below the ~10-11 mg/L seen in all three source batches at the same age, while product formation (P=2.61 g/L at 48 h) remains on trajectory. The limiting factor is oxygen transfer, not feed. A bounded 15% aeration increase directly addresses the DO deficit without sacrificing product mass or risking DO-constraint violation (it can only raise DO2). Feed reduction or stop would needlessly lose product mass; KEEP risks DO2 breaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum within hours.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process parameters (OUR, kLa) are unavailable, so the 15% aeration increase may only partially restore DO2; if demand keeps growing, DO2 could still approach the 2.0 mg/L floor and further action may be needed at the next routine assay. The DO2 drop could also partly reflect a sensor artifact, but its persistence over ~4 h across many readings supports a real deficit.
